messages.subject: random slope syntax in inlabru
parts:
I'd like to implement a spatial model in inlabru that also includes a random slope component (in lme4 form, it would look like y ~ x1 + (1 + x1|group)). I've looked at a couple other examples of this on the discussion group but I'm still a bit confused about the syntax on how to include this. Right now, my spatial model looks like something like this:

# setting up options
c.c <- list(
  cpo = TRUE,
  dic = TRUE,
  waic = TRUE,
  config = TRUE
)

# spatial model
mod <- bru(julian_lay ~ Intercept + x1 + site(map = coordinates, model = spde1),
    family = "gaussian", 
    data = as_Spatial(df),
    options = list(control.compute = c.c)
  )

But I would be curious to know how the slope of x1 varies by group. I'm guessing the 'group' variable will need to be converted from a factor into an integer for inlabru, but not sure what the required syntax would look like...

Thanks,

Jay

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] random slope syntax in inlabru
parts:
Hi,
I think what you're looking for is an iid model for the beta_x coefficient with one beta_x value per group?
You're right that you need the group to be indexed by integers from 1 through maxgroup, say mygroup.
I think this should work:

~ xeffect(mygroup, weight = x1, model="iid", n = maxgroup) + ...

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] random slope syntax in inlabru
parts:
False alarm, it works, but not with weights (except possibly some versions); instead, use the general R expression formula approach.
Here's an example:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
library(inlabru)
ngroups <- 20
nobs <- 100
data <-
  data.frame(x = rnorm(nobs),
             mygroup = rep(seq_len(ngroups), nobs / ngroups)) %>%
  mutate(y = rnorm(ngroups)[mygroup] +
           rnorm(ngroups)[mygroup] * x +
           rnorm(nobs, sd = 0.1))
components <- ~ -1 +
  intercept(map = mygroup, model="iid", n = ngroups) +
  betax(map = mygroup, model="iid", n = ngroups)
formula <- y ~ intercept + betax * x
result <- bru(components = components,
              formula = formula,
              family = "gaussian",
              data = as.data.frame(data))
INLA:::summary.inla(result)


Finn

2) Is it possible to include the spatial random effect with this type of model (and would that be included in the 'components' or 'formula' argument)? 

Thanks,

Jay

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] random slope syntax in inlabru
parts: On Thu, 13 Aug 2020 at 21:10, Jason Winiarski <jmwin...@gmail.com> wrote:
1) How would I go about extracting the average slope value and group specific slopes from the summary/model output?

The estimated latent variables will be in
  result$summary.random$b0
and
  result$summary.random$b1
(or whatever name use use for them) as for any other inla model. To get the posterior mean of the average slope, you can just take
  mean(result$summary.random$b1$mean), but for more complicated summaries, it depends on what you want to compute. The inlabru::predict() function can be used for more general posterior prediction.
2) Is it possible to include the spatial random effect with this type of model (and would that be included in the 'components' or 'formula' argument)?

Yes, I just didn't include it in the example, since it's unrelated to the grouped slope feature. You'll need to add a spatial component, and then add it to the formula expression as well.


Finn 
 

Thanks,

Jay
